Per Section 508 compliance criteria - 602.2 Accessibility and Compatibility Features: Documentation shall list and explain how to use the accessibility and compatibility features required by Chapters 4 and 5. Documentation shall include accessibility features that are built-in and accessibility features that provide compatibility with assistive technology. info Software is exempt from Chapter 4. Chapter 5 still applies. To access accessibility features on your machine, type "accessibility" into your search bar and click the "Ease of Access Settings" option. Applications such as Magnifier and Narrator are among these features. From this screen, you can select and enable the feature(s) you need to use. Windows-based accessibility features are compatible with TCMax®. It is worth noting that the use of such features is not always practical. For example, the Narrator application will read everything on the main screen of TCMax® but in no discernable order. The Narrator also will not read graphs and charts within TCMax®, nor will it read trackers within the Dashboard. As another example, increasing the size of the text on screen will only increase the size of the menus at the top of the screen in TCMax®. However, a workaround for this is to simply use the Magnifier.

info The ATC Sync Service has been deprecated and is no longer available for purchase. The information provided in this section is retained for reference and support purposes for existing installations. The Service Console allows you to start, stop, and manage the services that are installed on your machine. note You may not manage services on another machine over the network using the Service Console. Upon running the TCMax® Service Console for the first time, you will be prompted with a message asking you to configure your ATC connection settings. The Options screen allows you to configure connection settings to the ATC service, as well as your TCMax® Database. The Server Name is the name of the Server that hosts the ATC Web Service. The Service Port is the port that the ATC Web Service is running on (this will be set to a default value of 58010, as it is the default port for the ATC Web Service). Test Connection will test the connection to the ATC using the provided connection information. The Save button will save all changes that have been made in the Options screen. This interface is everything you will need to configure your TCMax® ATC Sync Service. When started, the TCMax® ATC Sync Service will communicate with this console via the log window to the right. File, Options, and About are different menu options that allow you to access different tools and options. The Sync TCMax® with ATC every __ section allows you to configures the time in-between syncs. The Start Sync Service, Stop Sync Service, and Force Sync buttons are utilized for starting, stopping, or forcing the TCMax® ATC Sync Service to sync. The TCMax® Sync Service Status section is a live log output from the TCMax® ATC Sync Service containing important runtime information such as errors and sync times. The Status section is used to view the current status of the TCMax® ATC Sync Service (not to be confused with the status of the ATC service). The Clear Log Window button is used for clearing the log window. On the Main Screen of the Service Console, click File > Import. The import tool allows you to import ATC boxes and log records into your TCMax® Database. You may also view your imported boxes and retool ATC boxes. In Step 1, Check ATC Boxes to Import, you can select un-imported ATC boxes for import. In Step 2, Select a Shop Code to Import Box(es), you can select the specific Shop Code you wish to import the ATC boxes into. In Step 2, Import Log Records, you can import log records from a specified start date, this is optional and not required. The Import button is utilized to start the import process for the ATC Box(es). The Imported ATC Boxes section displays all previously imported ATC boxes and their Shop Code. The Update ATC Box(es) button allows you to update ATC boxes after they have been re-tooled. Once the Import button has been selected a set of progress bars will appear indicating the status of the import. Please be patient, as this process may take a long time to finish on large installations of ATC. After the import process is complete, you will receive a message indicating that the import was successful and you will be returned to the Main Screen. You are now ready to start the Sync Service. To start the TCMax® ATC Sync Service, click the Start Sync Service button. You should notice that the log window to the right will begin to fill with log Data. If settings for the Database connection and ATC connection are properly configured, you should see that the service responds with a successful connection message. A sync will automatically occur when the service is initially brought online. If at any time you require that a sync occur immediately, you may click the Force Sync button to manually start a sync.

Before installing the TCMax® Service Console, be prepared to have the following resources ready: Access to a user account with administrative privileges A TCMax® Database that is of the latest version, or has been previously migrated to at least version 9.x. The TCMax® Service Console installer package. The ATC Web Service certificate file provided with your ATC software (AtcWsCert.pfx), and the certificate’s password. To begin installation, navigate to the location of the ATC Web Service certificate (the directory shown in the image below may not match the location of your certificate file). In the File Explorer, right click the file AtcWsCert.pfx, and click Install PFX. info The certificate file “AtcWsCert.pfx” is provided by Snap-On. Please contact Snap-On for assistance in obtaining a copy of this file. The Certificate Import Wizard will open. For the Store Location of the certificate, click Local Machine, and click Next. Do not tamper with the file name text box, as it is populated with the location of the file you chose to install. Click Next. Enter the password provided to you with your certificate file, and click Next. When prompted for the certificate store to install the certificate to, click Place all certificates in the following store, then click Browse. Leave the selected certificate store as Personal, then click OK. After selecting the certificate store, confirm that the certificate store is set to Personal, and click Next. After the wizard has completed importing the certificate, click Finish. The certificate has completed the installation process. Click Finish. You have successfully installed the certificate required for your machine to contact the ATC Web Service.

documents.t: info The ATC Sync Service is deprecated and is no longer available for purchase. This documentation is retained for reference and support purposes for existing installations. To license an existing Sync Service installation, the logged-on Windows user must have full administrative permissions, as the licensing process creates or modifies registry entries. To license the Sync Service, launch the Soaring License Manager by clicking on your Start Menu > TCMax® > Soaring License Manager. The machines UAC may request to allow this application to make changes to your computer. You need to allow this to be able to proceed (if prompted). Click on the Add / Modify button to add or modify a license entry. Select TCMax® Sync Service under Select Software to License and click OK. If you have not licensed TCMax® yet you will need to enter the Company Name, Support Id, and your Sync Service License Key. If you have already licensed your TCMax® software you will only need to enter your Sync Service License Key. Once you have entered your information a green checkmark should appear next to the license key entry area and you can click the Activate button to complete the licensing process. If a green checkmark does not appear, double check your information to make sure it has been entered accurately, the licensing credentials are case and space sensitive.

The TCMax® ATC Sync Service is installed to run under the Local System built in user account. For the Sync Service to communicate with your TCMax® Database, you must choose one of the following installation options: Option 1: Install the service on the same machine as your Microsoft SQL Server®, and grant read/write permissions to the NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM user account. (Windows Authentication must be used for the Database connection) Option 2: Install the service on the machine of your choosing and use SQL Authentication for the Database connection. Option 3: Install the service on the machine of your choosing. Create/choose a Windows user, and grant read/write permissions to your Database, then manually change the service to run as that user (Windows Authentication).

2fa The Service Console does not support two factor authentication (2fa). If you use two factor authentication for your email, you will need to generate an app password to use for the Emailer Service. Once you generate your app password, copy the password and that will be the password input for the email. Before using the Emailer Service, it must be configured to send emails from your Email Server. This process usually involves assistance from your IT staff or whoever oversees your Email Servers. To configure the emailer service, navigate to Options > Emailer Service from the Service Console. After selecting Emailer Service, an Emailer Configuration window will display. Refer to the SMTP Settings tab.

Display Name is the name of the sender for each of the emails that get generated. Email Address and Email Password are where you enter the credentials for the email account you would like the emailer to use. SMTP Host and SMTP Port is where you enter your email server’s address (you can enter the IP or the domain address as the host) and the port over which you’re outgoing emails are served. Send As HTML will send the email as HTML as opposed to plain text. Enable SSL will cause the emails to be sent out encrypted using SSL. The Send Test Email button will send a test email using the SMTP Settings you have configured from the Emailer Configuration window. You will be prompted to enter the email you would like to send the test to. Upon selecting OK, you will receive a popup displaying if the test was successful or not.

Display Name is the name of the sender for each of the emails that get generated. Sent From is the address that emails will appear to be sent from. This is optional and if not set we will use the provided Username. If this is configured, ensure the credentials used to authenticate to the Server has permissions to send with this address. Username and Password is the username and password used to authenticate to the Server. Username will also be used as "Sent From" if sent from is not set. Password is optional and ignored if use default credentials is selected. SMTP Host and SMTP Port is where you enter your email server’s address (you can enter the IP or the domain address as the host) and the port over which you’re outgoing emails are served. Send As HTML will send the email as HTML as opposed to plain text. Enable SSL will cause the emails to be sent out encrypted using SSL. Use Default Credentials will determine if emails should use the users default credentials. The Send Test Email button will send a test email using the SMTP Settings you have configured from the Emailer Configuration window. You will be prompted to enter the email you would like to send the test to. Upon selecting OK, you will receive a popup displaying if the test was successful or not.

Email Settings can be configured from the Service Console or from within TCMax® by navigating to Settings > Email Options. All the listed triggers will allow you to enter a Subject which will be the subject of the email and a Message which will be the message in the body of the email along with details related to the trigger.

Start by selecting the category you would like to setup automatic emails for. When expanding the category you will see the settings for the recipients along with other options such as Subject line, Message, Occurrence, Part Number, Report, etc. The image provided below will show the details and options within the Calibration category.

To choose the recipient(s), click the box Select Email Recipient(s) button and the Email Selection window will display, allowing you to select from Email Addresses added to your users. Simply select the email(s) you wish to assign to to the trigger and move them to the right box by selecting the button.

If you would like to provide an email that is not a current user in the Database, you can do so by selecting the Add New Email button. Click Accept when finished to return to the Emailer Configuration window.

Several of the email triggers have Part Number settings that can be implemented. In the grids that contain the Part Number and warning level, you can set it so that the email will only be sent if the number of items with the Part Number entered has reached the warning level. The Only send an email for the following part numbers checkbox will set a threshold for the emails to be sent out only for the Part Numbers entered into the grid that exceed the warning level. note Part Numbers are not required, and if the checkbox to Only send an email for the following part numbers is left unchecked than an email will be triggered for all items being marked as lost, broken, etc.

Several of the email triggers have a schedule that can be set. In the Email sending schedule, you can configure when and how often an email gets sent regarding the trigger. tip By not providing an Occurrence, you can configure an email to be sent one time on the date and time of your choice.

Lost Status will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Lost. Broken Status will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Broken. Unserviceable Status will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Unserviceable. Long Term Status will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Long Term. Reorder Status will send out emails concerning items that have dropped below their reorder quantities. The emails can be sent out either at a specific time of day or periodically, depending on which option you select. Issued Items At End of Shift will send out emails concerning items that remain issued out to a user once the end of their shift has elapsed. For this report to be effective you must be using the shift feature in TCMax® found by going to Settings > Shift Setup from the Main Screen. You must have the shifts created and assigned times and the employees must be assigned to a shift. You can set the amount of time after the end of the shift to send a warning email to the relative user and the amount of time after the end of shift to send out emails to the designated recipient(s). Calibration will send out emails concerning items that are overdue for calibration or becoming overdue within a window of days. Inspection Status will send out emails concerning items that are overdue for inspections or becoming overdue within a window of days. Transfer Alert will send out emails concerning items that have been transferred either into or out of the Shop Code that the email has been set up for. Secure Inventory will send out emails concerning items that work in conjunction with CompX® locks provided by ekProtrack to notify the user about unauthorized access and unsecured closures of the lock system. Custom Reports can send user generated reports as emails if the report requires no input from the user (parameters). You can select the report you would like emailed from the list on the left side of this section and input the recipient and email information in the appropriate areas. You can then set the date and time for the initial email as well as the schedule for the email. This section also allows you to Add Event(s) for the trigger. Allowing you to have a set schedule along with immediate attention after a specific trigger occurs. warning Any report that requires user input will not be able to be sent via the emailer. This includes mandatory barcodes, dates, or any additional parameters that TCMax® has built in or users have included in custom reports.

The TCMax® Service Console sends emails based on specific triggers in the TCMax® Database. The emailer will send triggered emails every five minutes. The interface above shows you the options you have available to manage the service. Once the service is configured you can start or stop the emailer service by clicking either the Start Emailer Service or Stop Emailer Service buttons. The Check Emails to Send button will display any queued emails that will be sent out upon the next 5 minute interval in the Status window. The View Failed Emails button will display any emails that were unable to be sent. The Clear Log Window button will clear any of the current entries out of the TCMax® Emailer Service Status window.

The File Menu will allow you to Import your ATC Certificate when utilizing the Service Console for the ATC Sync Service. The Import tool can also be accessed by press Ctrl + I on your keyboard. The File Menu also allows you to Exit the Service Console.

Selecting Service Console will allow to change your Database Connection. Selecting Emailer Service will allow you to setup your email triggers along with your SMTP Settings. Take a look at our Configuring SMTP Settings sections for information on this. Selecting Sync Service will allow you to configure your settings for the ATC Sync Service.

Save the file to your computer and once the download is complete, browse to the file and double-click to begin the setup. info Installing the TCMax® Service Installer will require the logged-in user to have Windows Administrative Privileges. Select Next on the welcome screen of the installation wizard. Read the Software License Agreement carefully. If you accept the terms in the License Agreement, select I accept the terms in the license agreement, and select Next; otherwise, click Cancel. If you do not agree to the terms of the Software License Agreement, you will not be able to install this software. Click Install. The Installer will require that you grant it permission after clicking install. Please be patient as the software installs. When the installer finishes, click Finish to conclude the installation of the Service Manager. On your first run of the TCMax® Service Console, you will be presented with a Connection Properties window where you will connect to the Database that the Service Console will monitor. Once you have successfully established the connection to the Database, proceed to the Introduction section.

Introduction to additional services for the TCMax® Asset Management Suite. Overview Software License Agreement Trademarks TCMax® currently offers a console for managing several server-side applications used for various operations known as the TCMax® Service Console. Services will be installed as a Windows service, and may be started, stopped, and configured via the TCMax® Service Console. Once installed and configured, the services installed will run autonomously without requiring you to manage them. The TCMax® Service Console currently allows you to manage the TCMax® ATC Sync Service. Previously referred to as ATC Sync/Bridge. The TCMax® ATC Sync Service syncs employees, issued items, logs, and more between TCMax® and ATC. You can also manage the TCMax® Emailer Service via the TCMax® Service Console. If the TCMax® ATC Sync Service is going to be used, the TCMax® Service Console is recommended to be installed on the server that is hosting the TCMax® Database. To ensure service uptime, we do not recommend installing the TCMax® Services Console on a user’s desktop / client computer. Only one instance of TCMax® Service Console should be connected to any given TCMax® Database.
